data.title: Carlyle Secured Lending, Inc. Schedules Earnings Release and Quarterly Earnings Call to Discuss its Financial Results for the Third Quarter Ended September 30, 2026
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Carlyle Secured Lending, Inc. (“Carlyle Secured Lending”) will host a conference call at 11:00 a.m. (Eastern Time) on Friday, November 6, 2026 to announce its financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. The Company will report its quarterly financial results on Thursday, November 5, 2026.

The conference call will be available via public webcast via a link on Carlyle Secured Lending’s website at carlylesecuredlending.com and will also be available on the website soon after the call’s completion.

About Carlyle Secured Lending, Inc.

Carlyle Secured Lending, Inc. is a publicly traded business development company (“BDC”) which began investing in 2013. The Company focuses on providing directly originated, financing solutions across the capital structure, with a focus on senior secured lending to middle-market companies primarily located in the United States. Carlyle Secured Lending is externally managed by Carlyle Global Credit Investment Management L.L.C., an SEC-registered investment adviser and wholly owned subsidiary of Carlyle.

Web: carlylesecuredlending.com

About Carlyle

Carlyle (“Carlyle,” or the “Adviser”) is a global investment firm with deep industry expertise that deploys private capital across three business segments: Global Private Equity, Global Credit and Carlyle AlpInvest. With $485 billion of assets under management as of June 30, 2026, Carlyle’s purpose is to connect people, ideas, and capital to fuel growth for companies and performance for investors. Carlyle employs more than 2,500 people in 28 offices across four continents. Further information is available at www.carlyle.com. Follow Carlyle on X @OneCarlyle and LinkedIn at The Carlyle Group.

data.title: Apple Stock Climbs as Its New Foldable iPhone Faces a Three-Month Wait
data.description:
Apple shares climbed 1% on Friday morning as delivery estimates for its first foldable smartphone slipped into late January, signaling an early supply crunch ahead of the device's retail launch.

The iPhone Duo, priced from $1,999, opens for retail sales Oct. 23. Apple's U.S. online store lists Jan. 29 as the estimated delivery date for models with 256GB, 512GB, 1TB and 2TB of storage.

The extended wait comes as Apple looks to expand its premium smartphone lineup with a foldable design. Counterpoint Research estimates the company could sell six million Duo units in 2026. The device features two batteries, a glare-reducing screen finish and a 48-megapixel Fusion camera.

Demand has also supported Apple's latest conventional models. The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max recorded 12% year-over-year growth during their first week in China, helping the company capture 33% of the country's smartphone market for the period, according to Counterpoint.

Apple recently joined Nvidia as the second company to reach a $5 trillion market capitalization. The company's standard iPhone 18, iPhone Air 2 and iPhone 18e are expected to arrive around March 2027.

data.title: Illinois American Water Announces 2026 "Water Keeps Life Flowing" Art Contest
data.description:
Grade school contest raises awareness of the role high-quality water systems play in students' daily lives

BELLEVILLE, Ill., Oct 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Illinois American Water encourages students to showcase their creativity by submitting artwork to the company's "Water Keeps Life Flowing" art contest. Entries from 3rd, 4th, and 5th grade students will capture what high-quality water service means to them, and artwork will be accepted through Friday, Nov. 13, 2026.

"Our annual art contest encourages students to bring art and science together to depict the importance of water in a creative way," says Brian Eisenloeffel, President, Illinois American Water. "We are excited to see what safe, clean, and reliable water means to our young customers."

Art contest entries open Oct. 16, 2026, just one day after the annual observance of the U.S. Water Alliance's Imagine a Day Without Water on Oct. 15, which encourages people to consider the devastating impact of a single day without access to safe, clean water.

Eisenloeffel added, "Water keeps our lives flowing by helping families, schools, communities, and the environment thrive. Water is essential for drinking, cooking, growing gardens, protecting public health, supporting local businesses, and helping firefighters keep our communities safe. Illinois American Water plays a critical role in customers' daily lives by providing water service that supports these essential activities and community operations."

Up to 10 winners will earn a prize pack, valued at roughly $100, to share with their classroom. Available prize packs include:

  • Creative Kids – art supplies like colored pencils, markers, crayons;
  • STEM Education – science trivia board game, magnetic tiles, Guess in 10 Animal Planet; and
  • Classroom Party – Uno Junior, 30 Fidget Toy Keychains, Would You Rather? School & Classroom Edition.

The winning artwork may be featured in future Illinois American Water customer communications. Past winning artwork can be found on the company's Facebook page: @ilamwater.

Additional contest rules and guidelines can be found on Illinois American Water's website under the News & Community tab.

About American Water

American Water () is the largest regulated water and wastewater utility company in the United States. With a history dating back to 1886 and celebrating 140 years in 2026, We Keep Life Flowing® by providing safe, clean, reliable and affordable drinking water and wastewater services to approximately 14 million people with regulated operations in 14 states and on 19 military installations. American Water's approximately 7,000 talented professionals leverage their significant expertise and the company's national size and scale to achieve excellent outcomes for the benefit of customers, employees, investors and other stakeholders. For more information, visit amwater.com and join American Water on LinkedIn, Facebook, X and Instagram.

About Illinois American Water

Illinois American Water, a subsidiary of American Water, is the largest regulated water utility in the state with approximately 600 dedicated employees working to provide safe, clean, reliable and affordable water and wastewater services to approximately 1.3 million people. American Water also operates a quality control and research laboratory in Belleville.

SOURCE American Water

data.title: Eli Lilly Discloses Investment at TRex Bio with 19.9% Stake
data.description:
SV Biotech Crossover Opportunities Fund LP acquired a 7.0% stake in TRex Bio, Inc.'s common stock. The fund bought 957,143 shares in the Oct. 8, 2026 IPO and saw 963,524 preferred shares convert at the Oct. 13 closing. The move positions the London-based life sciences investor as a notable early backer after the listing.

Investor Intent

SV Biotech Crossover Opportunities Fund LP says it invested for long-term value but keeps its options open. The fund may talk with other shareholders and TRex Bio’s leadership and considers “making proposals to TRex Bio concerning changes to the capitalization, ownership structure, board structure, or operations.” It also reserves the right to buy more shares, sell shares, or pursue “short selling or any hedging or similar transaction with respect to the shares.”

A 180-day IPO lock-up limits sales, transfers, and hedging unless the underwriters consent, which keeps the position stable through the lock-up period. After that, the fund and other holders can use registration rights to seek public sales through demand or piggyback offerings, subject to the agreement’s caps and timing rules.

Investor's Background

SV Biotech Crossover Opportunities Fund LP is a United Kingdom private fund limited partnership focused on life sciences investing. It is affiliated with SV Health Investors, a long-running venture firm known for backing biotech and healthcare companies across private and public markets. The crossover strategy targets late-stage private and newly public biotech names with a research-driven, long-term approach.

data.title: JPMorgan Stocks Rise After Buy Upgrade as Credit Costs Face Scrutiny
data.description:
Banking giant JPMorgan Chase rose to $341.75, up approximately 1.85%, at 11:17 a.m. ET on October 16, following a valuation-driven upgrade. According to The Fly, Freedom Broker lifted its rating to Buy from Hold on October 15 and nudged its price target to $370 from $365. Its reasoning was straightforward: the entry price had become more attractive.

Credit costs still deserve a close look. JPMorgan's October 13 earnings release reported a $539 million net reserve addition and $2.2 billion in net charge-offs during the third quarter, bringing total credit costs to roughly $2.7 billion. The standardized common-equity Tier 1 capital ratio stood at 13.9%. The reserve addition increased the cushion for potential losses; charge-offs reflected losses already recognized.

The valuation picture adds a wrinkle: shares trade 10.26% above the $309.94 GF Value estimate, suggesting the upgrade does not automatically make the stock a bargain. The reserve build accounted for roughly one-fifth of quarterly credit costs. The next test is whether lending returns can hold up without a sharper rise in provisions or actual losses. A higher price target helps sentiment. Sustained earnings need credit quality to cooperate.

data.title: Short Sellers Have Earned $32B Over The Past Week Amid Chipmaker Selloff: Report
data.description:
Key points:
  • Bearish investors accumulated roughly $32 billion in paper profits over seven days as the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped over 12% during an eight-session slump. 
  • Broad market indexes felt the ripple effect, with the S&P 500 on track for its worst weekly decline since June and the Nasdaq 100 sliding 5%. 
  • Short sellers betting against AI cloud provider CoreWeave Inc. netted more than $1 billion in mark-to-market profits following distressed debt signals and rising default risks. 

Short sellers have bagged a multi-billion-dollar payday amid a retreat in semiconductor stocks driven by CoreWeave’s debt concerns.

Short sellers recorded $32 billion in gross paper profits over a seven-day span as the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plummeted more than 12%, S3 data showed, as quoted by Bloomberg.

The sector benchmark, widely known as the SOX, extended its slump to eight consecutive trading days on Friday, putting it on pace to mirror its longest losing streak since 2006.

Market Anxiety Around AI Spending Persist 

The recent decline reflects growing market anxiety about elevated interest rates, lofty tech valuations, and the massive AI capital expenditures.

The selloff in chips has spilled over into broader equity benchmarks, setting the S&P 500 up for a 1.7% weekly decline, its steepest since June, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 dropped 5% in the week ending October 16.

Out of the 30 companies comprising the SOX index, 20 have lost over 10% of their value since the downturn began. Coherent Corp.(COHR) led the losses with a dive of nearly 30%.

"The run up in chips was very aggressive so invariably there was going to be some consolidation or pull back," Dec Mullarkey of SLC Management told Bloomberg.

CoreWeave Shorts Yield Massive Returns

Short sellers targeting CoreWeave Inc. (CRWV), an AI-focused cloud computing firm, logged over $1 billion in gains as the company's equity dropped more than 20% over the week.

CoreWeave's debt instruments slipped into distressed territory, with credit-default swaps indicating a greater than 50% likelihood of default over the next five years.S3 data noted that a portion of the short interest in CoreWeave stems from convertible bond arbitrage strategies rather than purely directional bearish bets.

"CoreWeave specifically is going to need a new story," Joe Tigay, portfolio manager of the Rational Equity Armor Fund told Bloomberg. "It's going to need time to digest this new reality."

The SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) dropped 1.2%, and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF (DIA) eased 0.5%. Meanwhile, the Nasdaq-100 tracking Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) fell 2.5% on Friday.

data.title: Tesla Has Built a Flying Car. It Will Blow Your Mind. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Al Root

OK, that was cool. And Tesla CEO Elon Musk wasn't wrong: People might not have believed it if they hadn't seen it with their own eyes.

Tesla unveiled the latest version of its long-awaited Roadster on Thursday evening. The event promised to be mind-blowing, and it was — the car flies. It flies. The Roadster event wasn't enough to boost Tesla stock on Friday.

Shares of the electric-vehicle — and flying car — company fell Friday by 2.1% to $354.72. The S&P 500 dropped 1% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 0.3, while the Nasdaq Composite stumbled by 2%.

The demonstration started with the car driving up a curved wall. Eventually, it was upside down. Then, it jumped off the wall, flipped over, and landed softly. Later, the car jumped over Tesla's vehicle lineup while spinning in the air.

It's a little difficult to describe. The car uses a vacuum to suction it to the ground. That will improve driving performance. Tesla said the car can turn a corner pulling two Gs (two times the normal force of gravity).

As for flying, the car uses thruster technology adapted from SpaceX. Ten nozzles manage 250 kilograms of air stored in special high-pressure tanks. The air tanks can recharge themselves; no special refueling equipment is needed.

The air thrusters also helped the car go from zero to 60 mph in 0.8 second.

The new Roadster was teased in 2017, almost a decade ago. It follows the first Roadster, Tesla's first car, which started selling in 2008 and was built on a Lotus platform.

Back then, the odds that Tesla would be a viable car company looked vanishingly small. That's obviously no longer the case. Tesla is the world's most valuable car company by a lot.

To be sure, Barron's didn't see a large chance of a big stock move. There is a limited market for supercars costing hundreds of thousands of dollars. Still, the car drove upside down and hopped over other cars.

Exactly what the car will cost isn't known yet. Production is planned for 2028. There will be three versions: a base model, a thruster-enhanced model, and a rocket model. The rocket version is "invite only." It's the version that can essentially fly. The thruster version will go from zero to 60 mph in under a second. The base model is a very expensive EV.

The event was also light on traditional EV specs. Battleroad research analyst Ben Rose was expecting a four-seater. The car has only two seats.

The Roadster is definitely cool, and a unique engineering achievement. All-In podcast host Jason Calacanis said recently that the event would "blow people's minds."

He wasn't wrong. Still, Tesla shares are all about AI now, with investors looking to AI-trained robo-taxis and humanoid robots for future earnings growth. (Musk said the Roadster would eventually be the last manually driven car Tesla made).

The event's lasting impact may be stronger ties between Tesla and SpaceX. Many investors and Wall Street analysts expect the two companies to merge one day, consolidating Musk's AI effort under one corporate roof.

The Roadster collaboration is the latest example of the two companies working together. They also collaborate on AI agents, semiconductor manufacturing, and power supply, among other things.

Write to Al Root at allen.root@barrons.com.

data.title: ASSA ABLOY sells PKI business unit to Vista Equity Partners
data.description:
STOCKHOLM, Oct. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ASSA ABLOY has signed an agreement to sell HID's PKI business unit to Vista Equity Partners ("Vista").

The PKI business unit (Public Key Infrastructure) provides digital trust, identity, authentication, encryption, and certificate management solutions. The business unit includes PKI SaaS - IdenTrust and HydrantID - credential management, and ZeroSSL.

"I find it very satisfying that with Vista, the PKI business unit and its employees and customers gain a committed long-term investor, creating new opportunities for the future and I wish them every success," says Nico Delvaux, President and CEO of ASSA ABLOY.

"Our PKI team has built a strong business with a strong customer base, and Vista has the expertise to take it forward as the market evolves," says Björn Lidefelt, EVP and Head of HID. "We are pleased with this outcome for our customers, our employees, and for HID."

The divested business had sales in 2025 of MUSD 58 (approx. MSEK 570) with a strong operating margin.

The divestiture is subject to customary closing conditions and is expected to close during the fourth quarter of 2026.

data.title: Blue Origin's Latest Move Shows How It's Quietly Taking On SpaceX — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Anita Hamilton

SpaceX has sucked up most of the oxygen lately when it comes to space companies, thanks in large part to its blockbuster initial public offering this summer. But let's not forget about the other heavyweight orbiting the space — Blue Origin.

An explosion this spring destroyed its New Glenn rocket during testing just a few weeks ahead of a planned launch, but that setback hasn't throttled the ambitions of the rocket company into which Jeff Bezos has poured $30 billion of his personal wealth.

Instead, the company is quietly laying the groundwork to become a stronger competitor to SpaceX's rocket business — eventually.

After reaching a staggering $140 billion valuation last month, Blue Origin announced Friday that it is investing $330 million in its "Rocket Park" in Florida to support manufacturing of the second stage of its New Glenn 9×4 rocket. That is its most powerful rocket, designed to carry over 70 metric tons to low-Earth orbit, used by internet satellites, and 14 metric tons to orbits, used by weather and television satellites.

The buildout will enable Blue Origin to create 150 of the rocket's upper stages. (The first stage, or booster containing the engines needed for liftoff, is reusable.) It will need them to launch satellites for Amazon and other customers like AST SpaceMobile, as well as to handle launches for the U.S. Space Force as part of the $2.4 billion deal it secured in 2025.

Of course, Blue Origin is still a long way from catching up with SpaceX, which has completed more than 700 missions in total, including more than 100 in 2026 alone. By comparison, Blue Origin has only completed two this year and just a few dozen total, many of which were suborbital.

But armed with new capital — it is raising $10 billion in its latest round, including $2 billion from Bezos — along with large contracts from the federal government, it's looking to get back on track.

While Blue Origin hasn't had a launch since April, Bezos said last week that the next one will happen in December. It's also asking the Federal Aviation Administration for clearance to conduct up to 50 launches a year from a single launch pad.

Don't count on an IPO anytime soon, though. Bezos said last week that might not happen for "several years," adding, "exactly when that will be, I don't know."

data.title: Ten-year yields set for biggest weekly loss in more than a year
data.description:
Key points:
  • LSEG data shows traders price 83% chance Fed leaves October rates unchanged
  • Markets price about 88% probability of December rate hike, LSEG data shows
  • US industrial output rises 0.7% in September against 0.4% economist forecast

By Sinéad Carew

Friday's choppy session put benchmark 10-year Treasury yields on track for their biggest weekly decline in more than a year, while investors assessed the latest economic data and bet that the Federal Reserve's next rate hike will not come until December.

After a tumultuous week when the 10-year yield swung between a high of 5.329% on Wednesday and a low of 5.037% on Thursday, the benchmark note moved between advances and declines on Friday.

But even with the day's moves, 10-year yields were still headed for their biggest weekly drop since the week ended August 1, 2025.

"There's a ton of competing undercurrents beneath the Treasury market that are pushing and pulling the long end of the yield curve in different directions and quite a bit of volatility intraday," said Michael Reynolds, vice president of investment strategy at Glenmede in Philadelphia.

He pointed to a "flight to safety" due to volatility in equity markets, driven by concerns about heavily indebted AI companies, and an increasing tendency by investors to look for opportunities in bonds since Treasury yields hit their highest levels in decades earlier this month.

On the data front, US export prices rose 2.2% in September compared with a consensus expectation for 1% and August's 1.2%, which was revised up from 0.6%. US import prices increased more than expected in September, boosted by higher costs for energy products and a range of other goods, offering further evidence of rising inflation pressures resulting from the Middle East conflict.

September's industrial output rose 0.7%, compared with economist expectations for 0.4%.

While investors have increasingly been betting that the Fed would pause its rate hikes, some were disappointed by the lack of guidance from Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh.

Warsh said he does not "prejudge" interest-rate decisions. But speaking at the 2026 IMF-World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, he said that with September's rate hike the Fed "made very clear that we would deliver price stability, and we removed a dose of accommodation."

Still, on Friday traders solidified their bets that the Federal Reserve would hold rates steady at its October 27-28 meeting, pricing in a roughly 83% chance of a pause while they put the probability of a December hike at about 88%, according to LSEG data.

The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note was unchanged at 5.087% after earlier rising to 5.1334%.

The yield on the 30-year bond (US30YT=RR) rose 0.5 basis point to 5.433% after trading earlier at 5.464%.

The 2-year (US2YT=RR) US Treasury yield, which typically moves in step with interest rate expectations for the Fed, fell 3.2 basis points to 4.719%. Earlier it had risen to 4.783%.

“So, there is some element really across this week of overcrowded trades and short squeezes unwinding to some extent. I don’t see anything that’s changing the fundamental trend direction in the case of yields," said Matt Weller, global head of market research at StoneX in Michigan.

A closely watched part of the US Treasury yield curve measuring the gap between yields on 2- and 10-year Treasury notes (US2US10=TWEB), seen as an indicator of economic expectations, was at a positive 36.6 basis points.

The 10-year TIPS breakeven rate (US10YTIP=TWEB) was last at 2.347%, indicating the market sees inflation averaging about 2.3% a year for the next decade.

data.title: U.S. Stocks Fall as Credit Fears Haunt Tech Sector
data.description:
By Rob Curran

U.S. stocks fell as fears mounted that artificial-intelligence profits would not come soon enough to meet increasingly expensive credit obligations for CoreWeave and other aspiring hyperscalers.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 175.28 points, or 0.34%, to 52002.41. The S&P 500 lost 84.62 points, or 1.09%, to 7659.44. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite dropped 572.99 points, or 2.14% to 26140.03, and lost about 4.5% for the week, its biggest decline since the week ended June 26.

Shares of CoreWeave fell 12% and are down more than 50% from their highs earlier this year as concerns about the cloud-computing company's ability to pay down debt lingered.

"Inevitably, with the cost of credit and capital rising to unaffordable levels, plans will have to be scaled back and capex reduced sooner or later," said Lorenzo Di Mattia, founder and chief investment officer at hedge-fund firm Sibilla Capital. Di Mattia has a modest short position on the U.S. stock market, he said.

Speaking at an International Monetary Fund event in Bangkok, Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh declined to give any rate guidance ahead of the October meeting of the central bank's rate-setting committee. Rising oil prices and broader inflation worries spurred long-term Treasury yields higher.

The yield on the 10-year Treasury note rose 0.011 percentage point to 5.097%. The yield on the 30-year bond rose 0.009 percentage point to 5.436%, recouping some losses from Thursday but still registering its biggest weekly drop in more than a year. The yield on the two-year Treasury fell 0.013 percentage point to 4.734%, completing its largest one-week retreat since August.

data.title: Reliance-backed Jio Platforms IPO: Rs.1 lakh crore gains for Meta, Google in Rs.30,213 cr issue by Mukesh Ambani firm?
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 16 -- Meta Platforms and Google could be sitting on nearly Rs.1 lakh crore in combined paper gains from their investments in Jio Platforms as the Reliance Industries-backed digital services company prepares to launch next week what is set to become country's largest-ever initial public offering (IPO).

Meta Platforms owns a 10% stake through Jaadhu Holdings LLC, while Google International LLC holds a 7.73% stake. However, neither existing shareholder is selling shares through the IPO.

At the upper end of Jio Platforms' IPO price band of Rs.1,119 per share, the two US technology giants could see returns of approximately 129% on their investments made in 2020, according to estimates highlighted in Groww's LinkedIn post on Friday, October 16.

The issue is entirely a fresh issue of up to 27 crore equity shares, with no offer-for-sale (OFS) component. This means existing investors will not sell their shares through the IPO. At the upper end of the price band of Rs.1,119 per share, Jio Platforms' IPO is expected to raise approximately Rs.30,213 crore.

Reliance Industries Group will become India's largest conglomerate by the combined market capitalization of its listed companies after Jio Platforms makes its stock market debut, Kotak Mahindra Bank founder Uday Kotak said on Thursday.

Unlike an offer for sale, in which existing shareholders sell their holdings and receive the proceeds, a fresh issue involves the company issuing new shares to investors. The proceeds therefore go to the company rather than to shareholders seeking to reduce or exit their investments.

In Jio Platforms' case, the proceeds are earmarked primarily for the full or partial repayment or prepayment of certain outstanding borrowings of its material subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm Ltd, along with general corporate purposes.

The structure means that existing investors, including Meta Platforms and Google, are not using the IPO to sell their holdings. Instead, the offering will bring fresh capital into the business while allowing these investors to retain their stakes.

Groww's accompanying graphic placed Jio Platforms at the top of its comparison of large fresh issues, with an issue size of Rs.30,213 crore. The graphic also highlighted the rarity of an IPO of this scale being entirely a fresh issue.

"The last was Reliance Power, in 2008," Groww said in the post, accompanying it with a graphic comparing some of the largest fresh issues in the Indian market.

The mega IPO will open for subscription on Wednesday, October 21, and close on Friday, October 23, 2026. The anchor investor bidding is scheduled for Monday, October 19. The company has fixed the IPO price band at Rs.1,065- Rs.1,119 per equity share.

The minimum bid lot has been fixed at 12 equity shares, each with a face value of Rs.10, with bids to be made in multiples of 12 shares thereafter.

data.title: Urban Company prioritizes InstaHelp growth as losses widen
data.description:
BENGALURU, Oct. 16 -- Urban Company Ltd is prioritizing growth in its instant house-help service InstaHelp over near-term profitability, even as its core businesses become more profitable. A year after its stock-market debut, the home-services platform is absorbing mounting losses to scale the offering.

Revenue rose 41.4% year-on-year to Rs.537.3 crore in the September quarter, beating Bloomberg's consensus estimate of Rs.517.1 crore. Net loss widened to Rs.182.5 crore from Rs.59.3 crore a year earlier, against an estimated loss of Rs.134 crore.

"Every segment of our business has scaled well, growth has stepped up," co-founder and chief executive Abhiraj Bhal said on the earnings call.

Consolidated net transaction value (NTV) rose 39.1% to Rs.1,432.3 crore, while orders more than doubled to 15.1 million. Annual transacting users grew 34.5% to nearly 10 million. India consumer services grew 26.3%, international operations expanded 66.2%, and Native, its home-products business, recorded 35% NTV growth, with festive sales shifting into the December quarter.

Penetration in Urban Company's largest service categories remains below 10% across the top eight cities, Bhal said, leaving room for expansion. The company is entering tier-two cities and improving availability, with customers increasingly able to find professionals within 30-60 minutes across its top 17 cities.

Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (Ebitda), excluding InstaHelp, reached Rs.30 crore, up 213% year-on-year. Core businesses generated Rs.119 crore in adjusted Ebitda over the past three quarters, up 175%.

"Our core businesses are now getting more profitable, expanding margins," Bhal said. India consumer services' adjusted Ebitda margin rose 110 basis points to 3.5% of NTV, while the international business's margin increased 190 basis points to 2%.

InstaHelp orders rose 63% sequentially to 6.23 million, but net order value fell to Rs.114 from Rs.138 in the June quarter. Its adjusted Ebitda loss widened to Rs.174 crore, taking consolidated adjusted Ebitda to a loss of Rs.144 crore. Loss per order narrowed to Rs.279 from Rs.346.

"I don't think the losses are high because of competitive intensity. Losses are high because we are choosing to keep them high," Bhal said. "We are choosing to invest from a position of strength."

About 45% of new users in markets where InstaHelp operates alongside core services now come through the offering. Customers include households needing replacement or additional help and younger consumers who book cleaning periodically instead of employing daily help.

Bhal said the category would need to become a primary source of household help to grow substantially, a shift he does not expect over the next three to five years.

Urban Company's steady-state model envisages pricing of about Rs.200 an hour and an average 1.5-hour booking generating Rs.300 in NTV. At payouts of about Rs.150 an hour to professionals, the balance would cover other operating costs. Current prices remain low, and some orders could decline as pricing normalizes.

InstaHelp could also drive more frequent app use, supporting Urban Company's ambition to become "the trusted home platform for Indian consumers, almost the operating system for the Indian home", Bhal said.

"The top of the funnel is not the challenge," he said of supply. The focus is on recruiting, training and retaining professionals, improving their earnings and maintaining service quality. Urban Company said supply-demand balance had improved, though demand still exceeds supply in some local markets. It has also launched instant services in the UAE and Singapore.

The company retained its target of consolidated adjusted Ebitda breakeven by the third quarter of fiscal ywar 2028 (FY28) and adjusted Ebitda of Rs.1,000 crore by FY31.

Urban Company's board approved a qualified institutional placement of up to Rs.2,500 crore, subject to shareholder approval. It ended September with Rs.1,901 crore in cash and treasury investments.

Bhal said the fundraise would provide strategic flexibility over the next five to 10 years, rather than meet immediate needs or simply finance InstaHelp's losses.

"The very definition of flexibility is that the sooner you do it, the more flexibility," he said.

The capital could fund acquisitions across India consumer services, Native and international markets, either consolidating existing markets or enabling entry into new categories. No deal is imminent, Bhal said. Asked about acquisitions in instant house-help, he said, "You never say never, but highly unlikely."

Urban Company is exploring residential air conditioners under Native, Mint reported in April. Drawing on more than a decade of servicing and repairing air conditioners, Bhal said the next one to two years would focus on learning and consumer feedback, with initial distribution concentrated on the app.

The company handles roughly 10 times as many air-conditioner servicing, repair and installation orders as water-purifier orders. Bhal said the launch should not materially delay Native's path to profitability, noting that research and development accounts for a substantial part of its current adjusted Ebitda loss.

Urban Company is also testing InstaHelp Gold, a premium offering. Bhal said initial results were promising but did not disclose rollout numbers or customer feedback metrics.
